title: Northshore AI - Hosting decision: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private (latency/throughput)
summary: Discovery call to understand Northshore's latency and throughput SLOs for a streaming chat product. Customer currently prototyping with in-house endpoints; evaluating Redwood Hosted for speed to market and Redwood Dedicated/Private for predictable p95 and data controls. Key asks: p95 <= 200ms for short responses, sustained 500 concurrent streams at 8 tokens/sec average, token burst handling, KV cache reuse for multi-turn, SOC2/KMS compliance docs. Next steps: run a 72-hour tokenflow benchmark, share security pack, schedule Dedicated sizing workshop.
next_steps: Redwood: share SOC2 and KMS whitepaper (Jamie) - by 2026-03-02
Customer: provide sample traffic profile and avg prompt lengths (Elliot) - by 2026-03-03
Schedule Dedicated sizing workshop with infra team (Priya + Maya) - week of 2026-03-09
action_items: Jamie Collins: send security pack and initial pricing worksheet (due 2026-03-02)
Elliot Brown: upload representative traffic CSV (due 2026-03-03)
Priya Nand: prepare Dedicated sizing draft after sample run (due 2026-03-10)
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-02-27
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Jamie Collins (Redwood AE), Priya Nand (Redwood SE), Omar Riaz (SE), Lina Cho (CSM); Daniel Park (Northshore CTO), Maya Soto (Infra Lead), Elliot Brown (ML Eng), Sara Kim (Product)

Auto-summary (auto): quick discovery, heavy on latency/econ, will run benchmark

[00:00] Jamie Collins: Hey everyone thanks for joining, I'm Jamie from Redwood Inference, with Priya and Omar on the call. Can you do quick intros?
[00:06] Daniel Park: Yeah hi Daniel Park CTO at Northshore, we build real-time conversational agents for financial advisors, low latency is make-or-break.
[00:12] Maya Soto: Maya, infra lead, I'm the person who will own networking and VPC stuff.
[00:16] Elliot Brown: Elliot, ML infra, I run our inference infra and perf tests.
[00:19] Sara Kim: Sara product, coordinating requirements.
[00:22] Priya Nand: Priya, solutions eng at Redwood, I'll dig into throughput and p95s.
[00:26] Omar Riaz: Omar, going to look at streaming paths and KV cache reuse.
[00:29] Jamie Collins: Cool. Goal for today is to understand your p95 targets, concurrency, streaming token/sec, and whether Hosted, Dedicated or Private makes sense.

[02:05] Daniel Park: Short version: we want p95 under 200ms for short assistant replies (like 40-60 tokens), and sub-500ms for longer streaming outputs up to 400 tokens. We expect about 500 concurrent live chats at steady state, bursts to 2k for minutes. Cost matters but SLA and data control matter more.

[03:10] Elliot Brown: Our current PoC uses in-house Triton endpoints; p95 is around 350ms for short responses under ideal load but stalls under burst. We're exploring hosted for quick ramp and dedicated for predictability. Also need KMS integration and audit logs.

[04:45] Priya Nand: Understood. A couple clarifying Qs: what's your average prompt length and expected tokens-per-turn? Also do you have many multi-turn dialogs that can reuse KV cache?
[05:02] Elliot Brown: Avg prompt 80 tokens, average response 60 tokens, multi-turns about 6 steps typical, so KV cache reuse is big for us. Also sometimes we include docs chunks so sequences hit 800-1k tokens for retrieval cases.

[06:20] Omar Riaz: That matters for batching and cache hit rates. If you reuse KV across turns we can keep latency down because the runtime doesn't re-encode everything. A note: our product is Redwood Dedicated for reserved capacity, and Redwood Private is the VPC/on-prem option — sometimes the transcript from our calls shows "Redwood dedicate" or "Redwood pryvat"— so apologies for any speech-to-text noise.

[07:10] Maya Soto: On networking side we have strict egress rules, need private peering or VPC with strict KMS. Is private deployment fully air-gappable?
[07:22] Jamie Collins: We offer a Private deployment option with customer-managed network, and we can support HSM/KMS integration. Not fully air-gapped by default but we have an on-prem packaging path for regulated needs. We'll share the SOC2 and KMS docs after this call.

[08:35] Sara Kim: For SLOs what happens during a burst? We need graceful degradation and fallback to a smaller cheaper model if full-capacity isn't available.
[08:48] Priya Nand: Right — we support smart routing and model fallbacks. You can define policies: prefer hosted high-perf model, fallback to cheaper/quantized variant, and we can throttle or queue. We also support prefix/KV caching which reduces token/time costs for repeated contexts.

[10:03] Daniel Park: Walk me through the numbers you typically see. For 500 concurrent streams at 8 tokens/sec sustained, what infra looks like?
[10:16] Priya Nand: Quick back-of-envelope: 500 streams * 8 tokens/sec = 4k tokens/sec sustained. For a 7B-ish model with high perf kernels maybe ~40-60 tokens per GPU-second accounting for batching efficiency and kernel packing; so we'd estimate needing X GPUs.

[10:45] Elliot Brown: X GPUs? Can you be more specific — that's vague.
[10:50] Priya Nand: Sorry, I'm being intentionally conservative on the call. For accurate sizing we want your token distribution and p95 targets. But ballpark: 4k tokens/sec sustained could map to roughly 60-80 TFLOP-class GPUs depending on model and quantization. On Redwood Dedicated we can pick specific instance types and tune quantization to hit p95.

[11:35] Omar Riaz: Also streaming latency isn't just model time; there's network hops, TLS termination, and prefix lookups. Our runtimes push KV cache to reduce repeated compute. For multi-turn reuse you'll likely see p95s cut by 30-50%.

[12:50] Daniel Park: We need p95 numbers at the token level. For 40-60 token replies we want <200ms p95. Can Redwood Hosted do that?
[13:05] Priya Nand: For Hosted, for short outputs and small models we often meet sub-200ms p95 in our benchmarks when customers are under typical load. But at sustained multi-hundred concurrency, Hosted will depend on burst capacity and queueing. Dedicated guarantees predictable tail behavior because capacity is reserved. There is a tradeoff: Hosted is faster to onboard, Dedicated gives predictable p95 and isolation.

[14:20] Elliot Brown: What about streaming token/sec benchmarks — do you have an existing bench harness we can run against our sample traces?
[14:30] Jamie Collins: Yes, we have a tokenflow benchmark repo we can run or you can run; it measures tokens/sec, p95, throughput, and burst headroom. We'll propose running a 72-hour tokenflow with your traffic profile to surface steady-state and tail behavior.

[15:05] Maya Soto: For private deployment, is there a difference in p95 compared to Dedicated? Sometimes private on-prem is slower because of networking.
[15:12] Omar Riaz: It depends — Private gives you control of your network and hardware. If you choose equivalent hardware and low-latency internal networking, p95 can match Dedicated. The common pitfalls are misconfigured NVLink, noisy neighbors on host, or storage hotspots for KV. We advise configuration reviews.

[16:40] Sara Kim: About caching — how does the prefix/KV cache affect cost accounting?
[16:47] Priya Nand: Cost is per-token generated, but caching reduces compute so net cost drops; we report token-level and compute-level billing in the console — you'll see cache hit rates and cost-savings.

[17:30] Daniel Park: Security checklist — SOC2, KMS, SAML SSO, RBAC, audit logs — yes?
[17:38] Jamie Collins: Yes we have SOC2, SSO, RBAC, and audit logs in Hosted and Dedicated. Private supports customer-managed KMS/HSM. We'll attach the security pack.

[19:00] Elliot Brown: A few technical deep dive questions: 1) how does Redwood runtime handle KV cache invalidation across rollouts? 2) what's the median warm-start time for NVCache? 3) do you support token-level streaming with function calls and partial outputs?
[19:20] Priya Nand: 1) KV invalidation is controlled by version policy — we can maintain KV across compatible model variants, and we do graceful drains during rollouts. 2) Warm-start depends on size of KV and model; typical warm cache loads are sub-second for small caches, but tens to hundreds ms for larger ones. 3) yes we support streaming tokens and partial outputs; function/tool calling is supported in the hosted API. Note speech->text sometimes wrote "function calling as fun-call" in some captions, so apologies for any weird words.

[21:10] Maya Soto: For burst to 2k concurrent, what is realistic fallback behavior? Queueing? Dropping? Re-route to cheaper region?
[21:22] Omar Riaz: You can set routing policies: queue with a SLA window, fallback to a quantized model, or route to a different region or Dedicated pool. We also have an autoscale burst that can temporarily increase capacity on Dedicated with preconfigured burst pools.

[23:00] Daniel Park: Can you share real numbers from a prior customer with similar profile? A short anonymized case maybe.
[23:08] Jamie Collins: Sure — one customer in fintech with 600 steady concurrent and 1.8k bursts saw p95 of ~180ms for short outputs on Dedicated with KV reuse, and hosted was similar at low load but p95 degraded to ~350ms during sustained 1.5k bursts. We'll redact customer name.

[24:45] Elliot Brown: For the tokenflow benchmark — what artifacts do you need? We can provide sampling of prompt lengths, tokens per response, parallel sessions, and connection churn.
[24:58] Priya Nand: Perfect, send a CSV with timestamp, prompt_tokens, response_tokens, session_id (anonymized), and a churn flag. We'll run the benchmark and return charts: p95 latency by token-length, tokens/sec sustained, and cold-start vs warm metrics.

[26:30] Sara Kim: Timeline: we want to pick a solution in 6 weeks ideally. We may pilot with Hosted first, then Dedicated within 8-12 weeks. Does that timeline fit?
[26:41] Jamie Collins: It's doable. Hosted pilot can be spun up in days, Dedicated sizing we'll need the benchmark then a 1-2 week provisioning schedule depending on region. Private will add more ops time (install + network), usually 4-8 weeks.

[28:10] Maya Soto: Any gotchas for VPC endpoints and TLS termination? We had trouble with certificate rotation and ALB sticky sessions before.
[28:20] Omar Riaz: We recommend mutual TLS on the VPC peering and our sidecar can handle rotation with no downtime. For session affinity we avoid long-lived TCP sessions; we prefer stateless short connections with KV lookups stored in low-latency store.

[30:00] Elliot Brown: One other question on metrics: do you expose token-level traces and p95 breakdown by model and route?
[30:09] Priya Nand: Yes the Redwood Console provides token-by-token cost, per-route p95, and tracing hooks. You can export logs to your SIEM.

[31:50] Daniel Park: Let's talk numbers again: if we need 200ms p95 for 60-token responses at 500 concurrency, what steps to validate?
[32:00] Priya Nand: Steps: 1) provide traffic CSV; 2) run our tokenflow benchmark on Hosted to see baseline; 3) run same workload on a Dedicated test pool with your desired model/quantization; 4) compare p95 and token/sec and observe caching effect. We'll produce a sizing recommendation with GPU-count and instance types.

[34:12] Jamie Collins: We'll also propose fallback policy configs in the recommendation: e.g., primary high-perf model + policy to route to quantized variant under >800 concurrent.

[35:05] Sara Kim: Pricing question: is Dedicated priced as flat monthly for reserved capacity + overage?
[35:12] Jamie Collins: Yes, Dedicated is reserved capacity with committed monthly cost and options for burst pools; hosted is pay-as-you-go per token. We'll send a simple worksheet showing estimated costs for your token volumes.

[36:30] Elliot Brown: For the benchmark run can Redwood run it inside our VPC or do we need to send traces out?
[36:40] Omar Riaz: We can run both ways. For the most accurate latencies we prefer running tests from inside your VPC against Dedicated or Private. For Hosted you'd run the client-side traffic from your network to Hosted endpoints. We'll coordinate with Maya to set up test endpoints.

[38:15] Maya Soto: Security onboarding — we need a point of contact and an NDA?
[38:22] Lina Cho: Lina from CS — we'll send our standard NDA and security onboarding pack. Jamie will include the SOC2 and KMS docs.

[39:35] Daniel Park: Anything else on model quantization and quality tradeoffs? We care about hallucinations when quantizing too aggressively.
[39:45] Priya Nand: We provide model-quality regressions monitoring. Redwood Optimize recommends quant levels per workload and includes eval hooks to detect regressions on your prompt set. We don't recommend extreme quantization for generation-heavy tasks without eval.

[41:10] Elliot Brown: For the trial, can we run 72-hour continuous load and then a 10-minute burst to 2k to see tail behavior?
[41:20] Jamie Collins: Absolutely. We'll include both sustained and stress bursts in the runbook. We'll also capture p95 and p99.

[42:45] Sara Kim: OK recap?
[42:50] Jamie Collins: Recap: 1) Northshore to send sample traffic CSV (Elliot) by 2026-03-03. 2) Redwood will run initial tokenflow on Hosted baseline then schedule Dedicated sizing benchmark (Priya/Jamie). 3) Redwood to share SOC2/KMS/security pack and NDA (Jamie/Lina) by 2026-03-02. 4) Schedule workshop week of 2026-03-09.

[44:05] Daniel Park: Sounds good. Any immediate blockers?
[44:10] Maya Soto: Nothing else — need to review the security pack.

[45:00] Jamie Collins: Great — thanks everyone. We'll follow up with calendar invites and the docs.

[45:15] Meeting end
file_notes: Transcript contains mild ASR errors (Redwood product names sometimes mangled). Customer prioritized p95 <200ms for short outputs and requested 72-hour tokenflow benchmark.
